handoff.purpose: Implements append_turn, append_roster, and declares load_transcript; contains sorting and roster validation logic.

symbols.name: append_turn
symbols.note: Convenience function that calls append_round with a single-turn list. Returns the chain hash.

symbols.name: append_roster
symbols.note: Validates and normalizes participant list, computes counts (requested, seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes, degraded), checks for duplicate classes, applies _scan_roster rule, and chains the roster record.

symbols.name: load_transcript
symbols.note: Declared only; body not in this chunk. Docstring says returns list of dicts, missing is [].

claims.text: Canonical body is the final tiebreak so the order is TOTAL even when two anonymised refusal receipts collapse to the same actor: chaining must not inherit wall-clock completion order from anywhere.
claims.why: The sorting logic using canonical_body_json is present, but the claim about 'anonymised refusal receipts' and 'wall-clock completion order' cannot be verified from this chunk alone; requires context of refusal receipts and overall chaining design.

claims.text: Convenience over :func:`append_round`; prefer the round form so ordering stays deterministic.
claims.why: The docstring references append_round and a preference for deterministic ordering, but the implementation of append_round is not fully visible here; the claim about ordering cannot be confirmed.

claims.text: Chain a single turn (a one-participant round).
claims.why: append_turn calls append_round with a list containing a single turn, effectively chaining a one-participant round.

claims.text: Chain the roster accounting: requested / seated / responded / unavailable with machine reasons, plus the DISTINCT INDEPENDENCE CLASS count and a degraded flag whenever fewer participants responded than were requested.
claims.why: The code computes and includes all these fields in the record dict.

claims.text: Counts are DERIVED here, never accepted from the caller: '3 of 4' and '2 of 2' must not be able to render as the same string, and a consumer that shows the participant count instead of the distinct-class count is showing a council of clones as a council.
claims.why: Counts like requested, seated, responded, unavailable, distinct_classes are computed from the normalized participants list, not taken from caller input.

claims.text: Duplicate weights are detected over everyone SEATED (that is when the clone was let in); the distinct-class count is over those who actually RESPONDED, because an unavailable participant contributes no voice and a class count that includes it overstates the independence on the record.
claims.why: The code computes seated_classes from outcomes 'seated', 'responded', 'refused' and heard_classes only from 'responded'. Duplicate detection uses seated_classes; distinct_classes uses heard_classes.

claims.text: Read all records, skipping a torn tail line (never fatal). Missing is [].
claims.why: The body of load_transcript is not in this chunk, so the claim about skipping torn tail lines and returning [] for missing store cannot be verified.

observations.what: append_turn delegates to append_round with a single-element list and returns the first element of its result.
append_roster validates phase in {'open', 'close'}, participant keys, actor format against _ACTOR_RE, and outcome against PARTICIPANT_OUTCOMES.
append_roster normalizes each participant with _norm_class and _norm_strs, and sorts by actor.
append_roster computes duplicate_classes from seated_classes, and distinct_classes from heard_classes.
append_roster checks _scan_roster and if truthy, replaces participants with empty list and adds 'refused' field.
load_transcript is declared but its implementation is not in this chunk; the docstring claims behavior that cannot be verified here.
